clues: This city lies in a wide basin in South America, on the banks of the Mapocho River. The high Andes rise to its east, and a coast range lies to its west.
Summers here are warm and dry, with long bright days and next to no rain. Winters are cool and wet, and they bring most of the rain of the year.
In 1541, Pedro de Valdivia founded this city to be the seat of his new realm. He laid out its streets in a neat grid round one main square.
From this city, the high Andes fill the east sky like a great wall of rock. On clear days, their snowy tops seem to tower right over the streets.
The president of Chile has his palace in this city. The top courts and the chief state offices work here too.
